parsed.explanation: No criminal statute touches trans identity (colonial provision struck, code effective 2020), no documented police targeting, sweeps or trans-specific violence (the only dated assessment says the community is not violently targeted), and courts have protected LGBT organising — a rule-of-law signal. Unknowns (border/document practice, custody placement, care access) are open questions, not exposures. No third-gender tradition or documented trans-specific acceptance is recorded, and resident-facing gaps (no LGR, repealed employment protection, no GI anti-discrimination law) weigh lightly as climate signals: institutions are neutral rather than trans-respecting, and society 'broadly neutral' with dated mixed attitudes. This resembles the dead-letter-law tier but without that tier's documented community acceptance, so it sits at the lower edge of reduced risk rather than its upper part.
